Calculate what's under the square root (the discriminant) first. If it's positive, you get two real solutions. If zero, one solution. If negative, complex solutions. Plug the numbers in carefully. Check your answers by substituting back into the original equation. Take it step by step - don't rush!

First, find the derivative f'(x) - that's the rate of change. Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x values. These x values are where the slope is zero.
